close_reason: Landed in c430f73 (paired with .7). Decision record in two places: (1) expanded comment on the from_raw_digest_formats_canonical_lowercase_hex test explaining why we don't compute the oracle via sha2::Sha256::digest(); (2) PLAN.md 'NIST FIPS 180-4 oracle for from_raw_digest tests' section citing the workspace test-integrity rule.
description: DEFEND ON REVIEW: digest.rs:267-278 test from_bytes_formats_canonical_lowercase_hex uses the SHA-256('') = e3b0c4...b855 vector from NIST FIPS 180-4 as oracle, with a comment marking it as 'independent oracle, not derived from this crate'. This satisfies the workspace 'No Test Integrity' rule (test vectors must come from an external authority, not the code under test). A future contributor who proposes 'compute the expected value at test time using sha2::Sha256::digest()' to make the test 'self-maintaining' should be refused: that closes the oracle loop, and any nibble-ordering or character-table bug in from_bytes would emit the same wrong digest the test expects. Keep this decision.
title: Sha256::from_bytes test oracle is NIST FIPS 180-4 SHA-256(empty) — defend the independent-oracle pattern
